title: Which instruction has to stall?

prereqs.why: You need the five stages and what forwarding can and cannot rescue before the stall is visible.
The reason a load is special here is that its result arrives a stage later than an arithmetic result.

statement:
A classic five-stage pipeline: **IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB**. It has full forwarding — a result can be handed from the end of EX or MEM straight to the EX of a later instruction, without waiting for WB.

Here is a RISC-V sequence that copies two values from one array to another, adding 4 to each:

```
lw   t0, 0(a0)
addi t1, t0, 4
sw   t1, 0(a1)
lw   t2, 8(a0)
addi t3, t2, 4
sw   t3, 8(a1)
```

Even with full forwarding, **one kind of dependency here still costs a stall cycle**. Click the first instruction that cannot start its EX stage in the cycle it otherwise would, and has to wait.
hints: Forwarding solves the case where one instruction needs a result the previous instruction has already computed in EX. Which stage produces a load's result?
Write out the stage timings for the first two instructions, cycle by cycle. When is t0 actually available, and when does the next instruction want it?
There are two identical copies of the same pattern in this listing. The answer is in the first copy.
